hooks.text: Earth's shadow does not cause the phases of the Moon.
Every phase of the Moon is just a shifting perspective.
Why does the Moon change shape every single night?

title: Why the Moon Changes Shape
description: Discover the real reason behind the changing phases of the Moon.

beats.text: Earth's shadow does not cause the changing phases of the Moon.
beats.visual: Full Moon phase near side features by LRO, 2011

beats.text: For centuries, a persistent historical myth erroneously blamed our planet for blocking the Sun entirely from our view.
beats.visual: Lunar eclipse blood moon photograph by NASA, 2015

beats.text: In physical reality, the Sun continuously illuminates exactly half of the lunar globe at all times without fail.
beats.visual: Moon phases diagram showing Sun illumination, Wikipedia

beats.text: As the Moon travels along its orbital path around our world, our observing viewpoint shifts constantly every single night.
beats.visual: Waxing crescent moon with earthshine photography, NASA, 2020

beats.text: This changing perspective creates everything from a delicate crescent phase to a brilliant full moon high overhead.
beats.visual: First quarter moon telescope image showing terminator, 2021

beats.text: Earth's actual physical shadow only touches the lunar surface during rare lunar eclipses occurring roughly twice per calendar year.
beats.visual: Total lunar eclipse photograph showing red moon, 2019

beats.text: Earth's shadow never causes the phases.
beats.visual: Full Moon NASA photography near side features, 2018
